reviewed_items.reviewer_notes: Code reading verified at subscriber_beacon_blocks.go:154. The broadcast call passes sidecar.Index (column index) directly as the subnet parameter without computing the actual subnet via ComputeSubnetForDataColumnSidecar(). The spec (SG-010 INV-002) explicitly requires publishing only on subscribed subnets. While mainnet has 128 subnets==128 columns, network configurations with fewer subnets would cause invalid subnet broadcasts. This violates the invariant and matches the spec requirement.
reviewed_items.spec_reference: SG-010 INV-002: Publishing only occurs on subscribed subnets (custody or sampling)

reviewed_items.reviewer_notes: Code reading verified at verification/data_column.go:527-547. The inclusionProofKey function builds a cache key using only KzgCommitmentsInclusionProof (4 elements, 128 bytes) and SignedBlockHeader hash (32 bytes), totaling 160 bytes. The KzgCommitments data being proven is completely omitted from the key. Two columns with identical proofs/headers but different commitments produce identical keys, causing cache hits to skip full Merkle verification. This is a critical cache poisoning vulnerability.
reviewed_items.spec_reference: SG-004 INV-002: Merkle proof links kzg_commitments to block body_root - cache must include commitments

reviewed_items.reviewer_notes: Code reading verified at verification/blob.go:77. ELMemPoolRequirements is explicitly defined as empty (line 77: var ELMemPoolRequirements []Requirement) with detailed comment (lines 73-76) explaining this is intentional due to the trusted relationship between CL and local EL. The spec property assumes semi-trusted EL, but Prysm's trust model treats the local EL as fully trusted for mempool blobs. This is a documented architectural decision, not a vulnerability.
reviewed_items.spec_reference: Design choice: Local EL is trusted for blob data per comment at verification/blob.go:73-76

reviewed_items.reviewer_notes: Code reading verified at rpc_data_column_sidecars_by_root.go:123-136. The by_root handler retrieves columns from storage (line 123) and serves them directly without re-validation. Storage contains mixed validation levels: RPC by_root columns (3 checks) and gossip columns (12 checks). The spec (SG-009 INV-004) states sidecars should only be served for blocks passing gossip validation. Whether this mismatch is exploitable depends on storage population logic and block validation state tracking, which requires deeper analysis.
reviewed_items.spec_reference: SG-009 INV-004: Sidecars should only be served for blocks passing gossip validation

reviewed_items.reviewer_notes: Code reading verified at reconstruction.go:150-165. The code calls kzg.ComputeCells() at line 150, then constructs proofs array by iterating exactly numberOfColumns times (lines 156-163). The CellsAndProofs struct at line 165 is constructed from the library-returned cells array and the locally-built proofs array. The code does not validate len(cells)==128, but relies on the c-kzg-4844 library guarantee. This is standard library trust, not a vulnerability. If the library violates its contract, all clients break.
reviewed_items.spec_reference: Spec silent on explicit length validation - relies on c-kzg-4844 library contract
